d: The biochemical maturation of sperm in the female tract that removes membrane cholesterol and glycoproteins, so sperm can bind the zona pellucida and undergo the acrosome reaction.
The outer, multinucleated trophoblast layer that invades the endometrium, opens maternal vessels and secretes hCG and human placental lactogen; it covers every chorionic villus.
The decidualized endometrium beneath the implantation site that forms the maternal part of the placenta; when it is deficient, villi attach directly to myometrium, as in placenta accreta.
A syncytiotrophoblast hormone, also called human chorionic somatomammotropin, that causes maternal insulin resistance and lipolysis so glucose and amino acids are spared for the fetus.
Unbalanced blood flow through vessel connections in a shared monochorionic placenta: the donor twin becomes anemic with oligohydramnios, and the recipient becomes polycythemic with polyhydramnios.
